title: AI-designed enhancers control gene expression in healthy mammalian cells
summary: CRG researchers measured more than 64,000 synthetic enhancers across seven stages of blood-cell development and found that enhancer combinations can activate genes in one cell type but repress them in another. The AI model used those measurements to design previously unseen regulatory DNA sequences that drove the intended cell-selective reporter expression in mouse blood cells.
ai_technology: Machine-learning enhancer design model developed by Lars Velten's group
organization: Centre for Genomic Regulation and Barcelona Collaboratorium

evidence.tested: CRG researchers measured more than 64,000 synthetic enhancers across seven stages of blood-cell development and found that enhancer combinations can activate genes in one cell type but repress them in another.
evidence.unknown: The enhancer designs are proof-of-concept reporter regulators, tested in mouse blood cells; this is not evidence of a safe or effective gene therapy. The paper's Cell page redirected to a cookie wall, so detailed findings rely on the CRG's linked official summary.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers used large-scale enhancer activity measurements in healthy blood-cell models to train the model, which generated synthetic DNA enhancers for specified cell-type expression patterns; experiments tested the designs in mouse blood cells.
